facts.statement: Cetarthrosaurus is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur found in the eastern United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Cetarthrosaurus is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur known from the eastern United Kingdom.

facts.statement: Harry G. Seeley named the genus Cetarthrosaurus in 1873, with Cetarthrosaurus walkeri as the type species.
facts.quote: Cetarthrosaurus was first named by Harry G. Seeley in 1873 and the type species is Cetarthrosaurus walkeri.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cetarthrosaurus come from the Cambridge Greensand Formation, dating to the late Albian or early Cenomanian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Cambridge Greensand Formation, dating to late Albian or early Cenomanian stage, of the Early Cretaceous-Late Cretaceous boundary.

facts.statement: Cetarthrosaurus belongs to the order Ichthyosauria.
Cetarthrosaurus is classified within the unranked family Thunnosauria.
Cetarthrosaurus lived between 106.3 and 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)
